title: How the V2 review bot works

scenes.text: How the V2 review bot works
scenes.subtitle: One merge request, from start to comment
scenes.narration: This video walks through the version two review bot, from the moment a merge request opens to the summary comment that lands on it.

steps.narration: A merge request opens, or gets new commits, and the webhook hands it to the review bot. Only repositories set to version two get this path.
Before any work starts, the bot claims the merge request, so only one review runs for it at a time.
Next it gathers context: the changed files, their impact on the rest of the code, scan results and dependency changes.
The review agent explores the code, records each issue it finds, and then submits its review.
The bot then counts the issues and computes the score in code. The model can only nudge it by two points, no more.
Finally, one summary comment is posted to the merge request with the verdict and the issues.
First the agent explores the changed code and reads what it needs, following the impact of each change.
Then it records each real problem as an issue, with its severity, category and confidence.
Last, it submits the review with a short summary. The bot checks the coverage before it counts the run as clean.

scenes.label: Every run starts at a score of one hundred
scenes.narration: Every review starts from a perfect score of one hundred, and points are taken off for each issue that was found.

scenes.title: Penalty per issue
scenes.narration: A critical issue takes twenty five points off. A high one takes fifteen, a medium one six, and a low one only two.

scenes.title: When the merge is blocked
items: Critical issue above the confidence threshold
High bug issue above the confidence threshold
Only open issues count against the merge
scenes.narration: A merge is blocked only by a critical issue, or a high bug issue, that the bot is confident about. Anything else does not block.

scenes.label: Files the agent must inspect for a clean run
scenes.narration: A run counts as clean only when the agent inspected at least eighty percent of the files it was required to read, or justified each file it skipped.

scenes.title: What lands on the merge request
items: One summary comment per completed run
Issues are listed inside the summary
scenes.narration: The merge request gets one summary comment per finished run. There are no queued or failure notices, and shadow runs post nothing at all.
